entries.title: The Holy Art Gallery
entries.description:
2 pieces exhibited in NYC 

1. Wanderlust 80x100x4 cm, Acrylic on canvas, 2024
A one-of-a-kind contemporary surrealist portrait exploring identity, curiosity, and the beauty of imagined worlds. Bold shades of crimson, magenta, violet, and warm gold unfold across a dreamlike landscape of oversized mushrooms and whimsical forms, inviting the viewer into a world that feels both familiar and otherworldly.
The central figure stands poised between fantasy and reality, embodying a sense of quiet confidence amidst the surrounding visual chaos. Through playful imagery and expressive colour, the work reflects the desire to explore beyond familiar boundaries, embrace individuality, and discover new versions of oneself. It is a celebration of curiosity, resilience, and the courage to wander beyond expectation.
-A one-of-a-kind original painting exploring feminine escape, softness, and the longing to wander.-

2. Reverie In Red Poppies, 25x25 cm, oil pencil colours & markers on paper, 2025
This one was more introspective and emotional. We described the figure as a pulse, crowned with red poppies representing memory, healing and the gentle messiness of becoming.
The earlier wording began:
“Reverie in Red Poppies” looks inward, into that quiet space where feelings and imagination mix.

entries.title: Arrival Gallery
entries.description:
Upcoming exhibition presentation in Madrid.

A Study In Presence, 30x40x2 cm, Mixed Media on Canvas, 2021
This painting began with a photograph by Rudi Huisman. Something about the woman's presence, her posture and her quiet expression resonated with me. I found myself drawn to the stillness of the moment and felt compelled to translate that feeling into my own visual language.

Rather than simply recreating the photograph, I approached it as a starting point for interpretation. Through colour, texture, expressive brushwork and shifts in tone, I began to move away from the original image and towards something more personal.

The process became less about capturing the photograph and more about exploring what I saw and felt within it. Somewhere between the original image and my interpretation, the painting began to develop a presence of its own, finding an identity beyond its photographic reference.

entries.title: Women Without Shame-Outique Gallery
entries.description:
To honour women's day, a group exhibition was held in Outique gallery - Lweibdeh, Amman, Jordan. 
2 pieces were presented in the exhibition.

1. Blooming, 35x35x5 cm, Mixed Media on Canvas, 2022
This work confronts the tension between control and release, where the body becomes both
a surface and a battleground. The lower half clings tightly, almost resisting itself, while the
upper form dissolves into textured made out of clay, sealed with resin, ocean-like matter. It suggests a shift from restriction to
fluidity, from containment to surrender.
The piece reflects the internal struggle many women face with body image, where discipline
can slowly turn into conflict, and care becomes entangled with pressure. The pursuit of a
“perfect” form often distances the self from the body, creating a quiet fracture that is not
always visible, but deeply felt.
The textured upper half introduces another language. It moves away from rigidity and
toward something more organic, more forgiving. It echoes the growing space where
acceptance begins to take shape, influenced by voices that challenge imposed ideals and
reclaim the body as something lived in, not controlled.
This work exists between those two states. It does not resolve the tension, but holds it. It
speaks to the ongoing process of unlearning, of rebuilding a relationship with the body that
is rooted not in perfection, but in presence.

2. Girl With Red Veil, 20x25 cm, Acrylic on paper, 2022
What does it mean to be beautiful?  
In our society women are expected to fit with the constantly changing 
beauty standards that have been set for them. Clear, fair skin tone, 
certain hair colour and eye colour, veil or no veil in hopes of controlling 
women’s body; molding women to erase their identity to fit the beauty 
standards. Different is beautiful.
